newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm, high-yields shed weakness.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm, high-yields shed weakness.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds posted a mildly positive reaction to the Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term rates unchanged on Tuesday, and spreads to Treasuries were flat to tighter in spots, dealers said.
Bids for high-yielding issues were lifted from early session lows after the Fed announcement, including some zero couponed telecom issues that had been underperforming, junk bond traders said.

Meanwhile, Chase Telecommunications Inc plans to issue $125 million in zero coupon bonds next month in the first deal of its kind since several like issues were postponed in March, according to market sources. The new issue could suggest the market is ready to buy after a hiatus and some downward price adjustments, said a head trader at a large New York firm.
"Zeros continued to be weak because people were worried there might be retrenchment in Treasuries and stocks, but now I wouldn't be surprised to that trend reverse itself," one telecom trader said.
But some zeros were still trading lower. Diamond Cable Communications zero coupon debt due 2007 was off almost one point to 58-1/2 bid, 59 offer, one trader said.

Elsewhere, high-yield prices rebounded to unchanged levels at mid-afternoon following weakness at the open. Inquiries for bonds accelerated in secondary activity but actual trades were few as the rapidly building new issue calendar captured the majority of the Street's attention.

New issues due this week that received strong roadshow interest are Stone Container Corp's $250 million in 10-3/4 percent senior subordinated debt with supplemental interest certificates and Navistar Financial Corp's $100 million in senior subordinated notes.
"Everybody knows Stone and people like what they're doing in terms of refinancing, and that helps them because they had a lot of stuff maturing over the next two years," one junk bond trader said.
Both issues should price later this week, sources said.
Activity in high-grade corporate bonds assumed a moderate pace after the FOMC announcement with best bidding seen for some media credits, including Time Warner Inc, according to one media trader.
The overall reaction was muted despite some improvement in market tone, traders said.

"(The FOMC decision to leave rates flat) should be a net positive for corporate spreads in general," one industrials trader said. "We've seen some better buying in the weaker credits but away from that not much reaction in high-grades."

In ratings news, Moody's Investors Service affirmed ratings of James River Corp, alleviating some fears that the merger with Fort Howard and an assumption of $2.4 billion in debt would prompt a downgraded to junk-bond status.
The agency said complementary product lines and cost reductions from synergies between the two companies were factors in the rating decision.
James River debt tightened about 10 basis points across the curve to levels last seen before the merger announcement, one trader said. James River 6.70s closed at 68 bid, 65 offer.
S&P affirmed James River debt on May 6, while adjusting its rating outlook to stable from positive.

In the Treasury market, the FOMC's decision to leave monetary policy unchanged at its meeting caused a runup in short-term rates and volatility in the long-end of the yield curve. Prices ended firmer and the 10-year note closed up 8/32 at 99-20/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
Analysts were split as to whether the Fed would leave the federal funds rate at 5.50 percent or raise it by 25 basis points.
